name: Isolated Congenital Syngnathia

criteria.description: Congenital bony or fibrous fusion between the maxilla and mandible
Absence of other craniofacial or systemic anomalies
Radiological evidence of maxillomandibular fusion on CT or MRI
Clinical evidence of feeding impairment due to jaw immobility

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of congenital maxillomandibular fusion confirmed by imaging without associated syndromic features
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical supported by imaging; genetic testing may be performed to exclude syndromic causes.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Congenital bony fusion of maxilla and mandible
searchTerms: bony connection between upper and lower jaw

pathognomonic.symptomName: Severe limitation or absence of mandibular movement

common.symptomName: Feeding difficulties due to restricted jaw opening
searchTerms: feeding problems due to jaw stiffness
difficulty eating because of limited jaw movement
restricted mouth opening causing feeding issues

common.symptomName: Respiratory distress secondary to airway obstruction

occasional.symptomName: Otitis media due to Eustachian tube dysfunction
searchTerms: middle ear infections from tube blockage
ear infections due to Eustachian tube issues
recurrent otitis media from drainage problems

occasional.symptomName: Speech impairment secondary to jaw immobility
searchTerms: difficulty speaking due to limited jaw movement
impaired speech related to jaw stiffness
aspiration pneumonia secondary to swallowing issues

laboratory: Generally normal laboratory studies; used to exclude infection or metabolic causes
imaging: CT scan showing bony fusion between maxilla and mandible
MRI demonstrating soft tissue involvement and temporomandibular joint hypoplasia
genetic: No specific genetic mutation identified in isolated cases; genetic testing to exclude syndromic associations
other: Clinical examination revealing absent mandibular mobility
Feeding assessment indicating oral intake difficulties

redFlags: Inability to feed leading to failure to thrive
references: Kumar, A. et al. (2019). Congenital Syngnathia: A Review of Clinical Features and Management. Journal of Craniofacial Surgery.
Smith, J. & Lee, R. (2021). Imaging in Congenital Jaw Fusion Disorders. Radiology Clinics.
